sentences.text: Thiesoscyllium is a newly described genus of carpet shark that comprises two new species.
Three fossil occurrences of Thiesoscyllium have been recorded in the database.
The genus was described by Delsate in 2026, according to the Paleobiology Database.
The genus is regarded as valid within the shark order.
Its type species is Thiesoscyllium underwoodi, and the genus also contains Thiesoscyllium felteni.
Thiesoscyllium is probably a member of the carpet-shark family Hemiscylliidae.
It belongs to the family Hemiscylliidae in the class Chondrichthyes, the cartilaginous fishes.
Fossils date to the Jurassic Toarcian to Bajocian ages.
Specimens have been recovered from Belgium and Luxembourg.
The animal lived between 182.9 and 168.6 million years ago, spanning those stages.
